description: Administrative roles face high AI exposure and uneven retraining pathways.
Skilled trades have lower substitution exposure but growing diagnostic and robotics augmentation.
Care work remains relational and embodied but faces monitoring documentation and scheduling automation.
Knowledge work is strongly exposed to AI augmentation and output-expectation shifts.
Platform work faces algorithmic control income volatility and limited social protection.
Production work faces robotics workflow automation monitoring and restructured task design.
Logistics work faces algorithmic routing pace pressure surveillance and robotics integration.
Education work may be augmented by AI but depends on human relationships judgment and care.
